summary: States RapidTO is being rushed and that projected time savings are unrealistic, with local residents, drivers, and small businesses bearing the impact.
source_quote: RapidTO is being pushed through under the guise of the World Cup — but even transit experts say the projected time savings are "unrealistic", and it's local residents, drivers, and small businesses who will bear the brunt of the impact.

summary: Supports better transit in principle but opposes the current RapidTO approach as a permanent disruption framed as a temporary fix.
source_quote: I support better transit. But this approach isn't it. If it's really about the World Cup, then let's treat it like that: time-limited, targeted, and actually effective. Not a permanent disruption dressed up as a temporary fix.

summary: States the proposal is a permanent reconfiguration of two major corridors being justified by six soccer games.
source_quote: What's being proposed here in front of us today is not a temporary fix. This is going to be rolled into a permanent reconfiguration of two major corridors, and effectively, it's gonna be justified by six soccer games.

summary: Raises concerns about the data and modeling used to justify RapidTO, citing transit commentator Steve Munro on Bathurst and Dufferin bus lanes.
source_quote: I have concerns about the data and the modeling that has been done here in an effort to justify this move... you can just read Steve Monroe on the Bathurst and Dufferin bus lanes who states, quote, a major problem with these claims is that the travel time savings will occur under, quote, worst case situations commonly in the PM peak, not all day.

summary: States that shaving as little as three minutes off the average transit trip is not worth the impact on businesses, residents, and drivers.
source_quote: even if the estimates are correct, I don't believe, as, you know, councilor Burnside was saying, shaving as little as three minutes off the average transit trip is worth the impact on businesses, local residents, and drivers.

summary: States council should proceed with humility, care, and evidence rather than steamrolling people, requiring transparency, data, and accountability.
source_quote: we have to proceed with humility, with care, and with evidence. And instead of steamrolling people, which is what our council seems to do all too often, we should be bringing people along. And that requires transparency, data, and accountability.

summary: Proposes following the 2015 Pan Am model: deliver RapidTO during the World Cup, then base long-term decisions on findings from the pilot.
source_quote: Follow the Pan Am model, which is what we did in 2015, which was successful, deliver it during the World Cup, and base our long term decisions on the facts and not a false sense of urgency.

summary: Spoke at council against the RapidTO proposal, arguing for a time-limited World Cup pilot rather than permanent reconfiguration.
source_quote: What's being proposed here in front of us today is not a temporary fix. This is going to be rolled into a permanent reconfiguration of two major corridors, and effectively, it's gonna be justified by six soccer games.

summary: Visited Bathurst and spoke with residents about their concerns regarding RapidTO including turning restrictions, traffic bottlenecks, and parking.
source_quote: I went out to to Bathurst, and I I spoke with some of those residents. And they do have concerns about ingress and egress of their neighborhoods, getting home at the end of the day with the turning restrictions, the traffic bottlenecks, the rush hour gridlock, the impact on those businesses in parking, trying to get their kids to the rink.

quote_text: Not a permanent disruption dressed up as a temporary fix.

source_quote: The Bubble Zone by-law has finally PASSED. ✅ After over a year of hard work, we've secured stronger protections for schools, daycares, and places of worship.

summary: States that keeping residents safe is the number one job of local government.
source_quote: Job #1 of local government is to keep residents safe. All residents.

summary: Supports a bylaw creating safe access/bubble zones around places of worship, schools, and daycares.
source_quote: a bylaw to protect people when accessing places of worship, schools, and daycares — free from hate, harassment, or fear.

summary: Opposes the bylaw's requirement that communities be victimized before qualifying for protection.
source_quote: removing the requirement for communities to be victimized before qualifying for protection

source_quote: Today, we hosted our second roundtable meeting for the Missing Middle Advisory Group at City Hall.

summary: States Toronto traffic congestion is a serious problem, with drivers spending 63 hours/year in traffic and bottlenecks costing the region an estimated $11 billion/year.
source_quote: Toronto drivers spent an average of 63 hours a year stuck in traffic in 2023, a 3% increase from pre-pandemic levels... These delays aren't just inconvenient—they're costing the Toronto region an estimated $11 billion per year in lost productivity and opportunity costs.

summary: States the city must prioritize faster construction timelines, better planning, and improved coordination to minimize disruptions.
source_quote: The city must prioritize faster construction timelines, better planning, and improved coordination to minimize disruptions while ensuring cost-effectiveness.

summary: States the status quo on road repairs isn't working and city leaders need a proactive approach to reduce construction-related congestion.
source_quote: The status quo isn't working. If Toronto is going to thrive and remain competitive, city leaders need a proactive approach to road repairs and reducing the chaos affecting everyone.

summary: States gridlock has tangible costs for small-business owners, reducing family time and productivity.
source_quote: For small-business owners, the cost of gridlock is tangible—more hours spent in traffic means less time spent with family and lower productivity.

summary: Brought a motion for 24/7 construction at the Gardiner Expressway, which passed at City Council earlier in 2024.
source_quote: Earlier this year, my motion for 24/7 construction at the Gardiner Expressway was passed at City Council, marking a step in the right direction.

quote_text: Toronto deserves a smoother, more reliable infrastructure strategy, and it's time to deliver.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States that housing projects below 12 storeys on Avenues served by frequent transit are not practically or financially feasible.
source_quote: projects below 12 stories on our our avenues are just not really practically or financially feasible right now

summary: Supports the new as-of-right zoning for 6-11 storey buildings on Avenues as a good step but says it does not go far enough.
source_quote: This is a good thing, and a good step - but it doesn't go far enough.

summary: States that for housing to get built it needs to be financially feasible — 'the math needs to work'.
source_quote: in order for that to happen, it needs to be financially feasible to do it. The math needs to work.

pledge_text: Will continue working to get more housing built and tackle the housing crisis.
source_quote: Together, we can get more housing built and tackle our housing crisis.

summary: Introduced a motion asking staff to explore increasing as-of-right zoning to 12 storeys on Avenues served by frequent transit; staff to report back early in the new year.
source_quote: I introduced a motion asking staff to explore increasing that threshold to 12 stories in areas served by frequent transit... They'll report back early in the new year with their advice on where that could make sense.

summary: Council approved new as-of-right zoning for Avenues allowing 6 to 11-storey buildings in places where they were not previously allowed.
source_quote: Last week, Council approved new as-of-right zoning for Avenues across our city. Now, folks can build between 6 and 11-storey buildings in a lot of places where they weren't previously allowed to.

summary: As former chair of Planning and Housing, authored the Housing Action Plan with recommendations to address housing barriers since amalgamation.
source_quote: I was the chair of planning and housing. We had penned the housing action plan, which provided a bunch of recommendations to sort of unpack and fix some of these issues that have been holding housing back here in the city since amalgamation.

quote_text: We all agree we need to get more housing built in Toronto. But in order for that to happen, it needs to be financially feasible to do it. The math needs to work.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States decisions about bike lanes should be made at City Hall, not by the province.
source_quote: These decisions should be made at City Hall, but we need to make the right ones.

summary: States the Mayor has not spoken with the Premier or province about the bike lane removal proposal despite publicly framing herself as standing up to the province.
source_quote: I was STUNNED to learn today at Council that she has not had a single conversation with the Premier, or anyone else at the province, about this proposal.

summary: States that without strong leadership and willingness to admit mistakes, provincial intervention in city matters should not be a surprise.
source_quote: without strong leadership, or the common sense and humility to admit when we've made a mistake, it shouldn't be a surprise when the province decides to step in.

summary: Questioned the Mayor at Council on whether she had spoken with the Premier or province about the proposal to remove Bloor Street West bike lanes; she answered no.
source_quote: Have you had any conversations with the premier or anyone else at the province about their proposals to move the bike lanes on Bloor Street West? No.

quote_text: How can she stand up for the city when she won't even speak up?
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States that Council's new investments in arts come too late, after a year of arts organizations scaling back, laying off staff, or closing.
source_quote: Council just adopted a new Council Plan - but these investments come too late for too many. Toronto's arts communities have been struggling this year - with organizations scaling back programming, laying off staff, or shutting their doors.

summary: Supports the new Culture Plan that will deliver funding for the Toronto Arts Council and Local Arts Service Organizations.
source_quote: I'm glad to support the new Culture Plan that will finally deliver that funding for the TAC and the LASOs.

summary: States the arts community deserved support from the outset and expresses regret for organizations and artists who suffered during the delay.
source_quote: our arts community deserved this support from day one, and I am sorry for the organizations, artists and leaders who have had to unnecessarily suffer this past year.

pledge_text: Commits to keeping the city accountable to ensure consistent support for the arts sector.
source_quote: Let's keep the city accountable, ensuring action when it's needed to support our arts sector year-in and year-out.

summary: Introduced motions during February budget debate to increase funding for the Toronto Arts Council and Local Arts Service Organizations.
source_quote: during February's Budget debate, I introduced motions to increase funding for the Toronto Arts Council and Local Arts Service Organizations (LASOs)... Unfortunately, the Mayor and her allies voted down that motion

summary: Supported adoption of the new Council Plan / Culture Plan delivering funding for TAC and LASOs.
source_quote: Council just adopted a new Council Plan... I'm glad to support the new Culture Plan that will finally deliver that funding for the TAC and the LASOs.

source_quote: It was an honour to present their Pledge of Unity against Antisemitism at Council this morning, and welcome them to City Hall.

source_quote: Harassment and threats against Jewish-owned businesses, fueled by nothing but hate, are utterly unacceptable.

summary: States the community must remain together in the fight against antisemitism and speak up against hate.
source_quote: We must remain together in this fight against Antisemitism. It's time to speak up and stand against hate.

source_quote: This morning, I was honoured to join the Remembrance Day Parade and Ceremony at Kew Gardens.

summary: States it is crucial to speak up and stand against antisemitism, citing attacks in Amsterdam and incidents in Toronto.
source_quote: Now more than ever — from the violent attacks on Amsterdam to the hideous forms of antisemitism in Toronto, it's crucial that we speak up and stand shoulder to shoulder against hate.

summary: States solidarity with the Jewish community and emphasizes the importance of remembering Holocaust history.
source_quote: we also stand in solidarity with the Jewish community

summary: States current interpretation of zoning rules is at odds with the spirit and intention of the policy and that confusion and red tape should not hold housing back.
source_quote: The interpretation is at odds with the spirit and intention of the policy. We cannot afford to let confusion and red tape hold us back.

summary: States housing is a necessity, not a luxury, and calls for action.
source_quote: Housing is a necessity, not a luxury. It's time to act.

summary: Brought a motion calling on city staff to review and amend multiplex zoning policies to address conflicting interpretations.
source_quote: My motion calls on city staff to review and amend these policies to ensure we stay on track and keep building the housing this city desperately needs.

quote_text: Housing is a necessity, not a luxury. It's time to act.
speaker: Brad Bradford

quote_text: It's time to focus on getting results, not just interpreting the rules.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States it is imperative to be vocal and unwavering in support of the Jewish community amid rising antisemitism in Toronto and worldwide.
source_quote: Now more than ever, with the growing waves of antisemitism in Toronto and the world, it is imperative to be vocal, proud, and unwavering in our support for the Jewish community.

summary: States everyone must do their part to combat hate and uphold Canadian values of equality and respect.
source_quote: we must all do our part to combat hate and ensure that the Canadian values of equality and respect for all are upheld, by everyone.

topic_focus: Holocaust education and standing against antisemitism
source_quote: This evening marked the beginning of Holocaust Education Week, here in Toronto. I had the honour of touring the Toronto Holocaust Museum, and hearing the stories of many of the survivors who came to Canada after the war.

quote_text: Don't be a bystander.

summary: States that arts are integral to Toronto's identity and that the city must continue supporting local creative communities.
source_quote: The arts have always been integral to Toronto's identity, and we must continue to support our local creative communities that make our city a vibrant, diverse cultural hub on the global stage.

source_quote: I had the pleasure of meeting with representatives from @tapa_to, @toronto_fringe Festival, and @iatse58 to discuss ways of fostering arts and culture in Toronto.

summary: States zoning by-law interpretations are complicated and inconsistent, creating challenges for people trying to build housing.
source_quote: This highlights the challenges for people trying to build housing and facing complicated and seemingly inconsistent interpretations of zoning by-laws.

summary: States it should be simpler to build the kinds of housing the city says it wants.
source_quote: We need to make it simpler to build the kind of housing we say we want.

pledge_text: Will keep fighting until every Torontonian has a place to call home.
source_quote: Every Torontonian deserves a place to call home, and I will keep fighting until this becomes a reality for all.

summary: Brought motion at Planning and Housing Committee to clear zoning confusion, boost missing middle housing, address multiplex permission gaps, and eliminate barriers to diverse housing options. Adopted Oct 30, 2024.
source_quote: Yesterday, on October 30, 2024, the Planning and Housing Committee adopted my motion.

summary: States that Toronto must use every tool available to increase housing supply amid the housing crisis.
source_quote: amidst the housing crisis with all the supply challenges in front of us, it is imperative that we use every tool in the toolbox to get that done to get more housing online for Torontonians and would be Torontonians

summary: Opposes piecemeal/site-by-site zoning approach in favour of comprehensive as-of-right permissions.
source_quote: we're moving away from a piecemeal approach to exclusionary zoning. This creates a comprehensive framework that allows growth where it's most needed.

summary: Supports expanding mid-rise development on avenues without requiring site-specific zoning approvals.
source_quote: This change will enable and expand mid rise development on our avenues without the need for site specific zoning approval

pledge_text: Will continue pushing for housing policy changes in Toronto.
source_quote: This is a step in the right direction, and I will keep pushing for the changes our city desperately needs.

summary: Brought a motion directing City staff to enhance work on increasing height permissions along Avenues with rapid transit, such as Queen Street East.
source_quote: My latest motion directs City staff to enhance their work on increasing height permissions along key Avenues with rapid transit like Queen Street. This could unlock tens of thousands of new homes

quote_text: It is imperative that we use every tool in the toolbox to get more housing online for Torontonians and would-be Torontonians.
speaker: Brad Bradford

source_quote: Year over year, housing starts are down 75% in August and 81% in September. With current market condition, builders aren't able to get shovels in the ground.

summary: States the City's new proposal to spur purpose-built rental construction falls far short of what is needed and will only help one or two projects already with other government funding.
source_quote: The City released a new proposal today that aims to address those challenges and get purpose-built rental homes built... but unfortunately, it falls far short of what is needed. This may help one or two projects that have already secured other government funding and are probably on public land

summary: States the proposal does nothing for more than 20,000 privately-led purpose-built rental homes and 11,500 condos that are stuck.
source_quote: it does nothing for the more than 20,000 privately-led purpose built rental homes and 11,500 condos that are stuck right now

summary: Opposes the Mayor adding another $8.3 billion to the funding wish-list from the province and federal government instead of addressing urgent housing issues.
source_quote: Instead of addressing these urgent issues, the Mayor just added another $8.3 billion to the wish-list of funding from the province and federal government.

summary: States a bigger move is needed to address the financial viability of housing projects, and expresses disappointment that this was not brought forward.
source_quote: We really needed to have a bigger move to address the financial viability of these projects, and I'm disappointed because that's not what was brought forward today.

summary: States the Mayor needs to be honest with people about the numbers when dealing with the housing crisis, characterizing the multi-billion-dollar ask of other governments as 'not real'.
source_quote: that's not real. And I think, you know, the mayor, when we're dealing with the housing crisis, needs to be honest with people about those numbers.

quote_text: In Toronto right now, housing starts have been more like housing stops.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States Toronto needs more housing ambition and that current staff proposals for the Avenues are insufficient to address the housing crisis.
source_quote: We need more housing ambition - period. Staff brought forward a report to allow more homes to be built on Avenues. It's a good step, but I'm concerned it still won't be enough to get projects moving and respond to the housing crisis that continues to grip Toronto.

summary: Supports raising height and density permissions along rapid transit corridors like Queen Street West, updating older study areas, and adding more mixed-use buildings along the Avenues.
source_quote: I've asked staff to go back to raise the bar on height and density permissions, especially along rapid transit corridors like Queen Street West; bringing older, outdated study areas up to date; and bringing more mixed-use buildings along the Avenues.

pledge_text: Commits to continue working to tackle Toronto's housing crisis with urgency.
source_quote: We will always keep working to tackle our housing crisis with the urgency it deserves.

summary: Asked city staff to revise the Avenues report to raise height and density permissions, update outdated study areas, and include more mixed-use buildings.
source_quote: That's why I've asked staff to go back to raise the bar on height and density permissions, especially along rapid transit corridors like Queen Street West; bringing older, outdated study areas up to date; and bringing more mixed-use buildings along the Avenues.

quote_text: We need more housing ambition - period.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States the city should waive fees for purpose-built rental housing.
source_quote: There's a lot more the city can do to enable the housing we need, including waiving fees for purpose-built rental and converting underutilized office spaces into homes.

summary: Supports converting underutilized office spaces into homes.
source_quote: converting underutilized office spaces into homes

summary: States the housing crisis must be tackled quickly; solutions cannot wait.
source_quote: We need to tackle this at speed. Solutions can't wait.

pledge_text: Commits to working toward making Toronto a place where everyone can afford to live.
source_quote: Let's keep things going. Let's make Toronto a place where everyone can afford to live.

source_quote: Grateful for the opportunity to join Developing Leaders from @torontonaiop yesterday to discuss critical housing issues in Toronto.

summary: States the bike lane debate should not be all-or-nothing; supports thoughtful urban planning and an effective bike lane structure.
source_quote: The answer isn't bike lanes everywhere or no bike lanes. It needs to be about thoughtful urban planning and an effective bike lane structure.

summary: States good bike lanes require safety, sensible design, and genuine community consultation.
source_quote: Good bike lanes begin with safety and sensible design, grounded in genuine community consultation.

summary: States that poorly designed bike lanes jeopardize their purpose of providing safe alternatives.
source_quote: When bike lanes fail to meet these essential standards, we jeopardize their primary purpose: providing safe alternatives for people.

summary: States Toronto has some well-designed, well-consulted bike lanes with strong ridership, and others with problematic designs and low usage.
source_quote: there's lots of examples here in the city of Toronto where we have fantastic bike lanes... We also have bike lanes that, you know, don't meet that merit of safe and sensible.

summary: States Toronto can only make progress at the speed at which public trust can be built, and poorly built bike lanes compromise that trust.
source_quote: in Toronto, we can only make progress at the speed at which we can build trust, and you compromise that trust with the public... when you try and tell them that something's working and clearly their day to day experiences that it isn't.

pledge_text: Commits to prioritizing effective bike lane solutions and rebuilding public trust with Torontonians.
source_quote: it's our responsibility to prioritize effective solutions and work to rebuild public trust among Torontonians.

pledge_text: Commits to focusing on bike lanes that work well and improving them further.
source_quote: We need to focus on doing the ones that work well, doing them even better.

quote_text: In Toronto, we can only make progress at the speed at which we can build trust.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States Toronto must once again become a safe place for everyone and calls out rising antisemitism.

summary: States the core issue behind Toronto's housing struggle is outdated zoning and insufficient supply.

summary: Observes that ~50,000 people, many of them families, left Toronto last year due to affordability.
source_quote: Board of Trade pointed out last year, 50,000 folks, many families actually picked up and left Toronto in a flight for affordability.

summary: States that the people leaving Toronto are key contributors to the economy, while those needing extra services remain concentrated in the city.
source_quote: We have a concentration of people who need extra help, need those services and supports that are often found in the city. But the people who are leaving are the ones that are key to our economy.

summary: Supports modular homes and faster housing solutions to improve affordability.

summary: States Toronto needs leadership change and a 'culture of yes' within the bureaucracy instead of roadblocks.

summary: States that different types of housing have long been 'off limits' to build in Toronto.
source_quote: Supply of housing that people can afford and the different types of housing that for a long time in cities like Toronto has really been off limits for people to build.

summary: States he spent time in the Chief Planner's Office at the City of Toronto, which motivated him to seek leadership change.

summary: States Toronto government should cut bureaucracy and prioritize delivering affordable housing.

summary: States the City of Toronto's priorities are scattered and government is reactive rather than proactive.

summary: Supports setting up an environment with opportunities for both market and not-for-profit housing sectors to thrive.
source_quote: when it comes to housing, setting up an environment where there are opportunities for growth, opportunity for market and not for not for profit sector to to thrive

summary: Supports aligning bureaucratic stage gates, divisions, and commenting partners to get applications to 'yes' as quickly as possible.

summary: States the most important change is empowering people within government to make decisions and drive projects forward.

summary: States that Toronto's zoning and planning approach since amalgamation is no longer working and needs to change.

summary: States homeownership remains central to the Canadian dream and that he is not ready to give up on it.

summary: Observes that housing has become an unavoidable topic of everyday conversation in Toronto, indicating a breaking point.

source_quote: you know that I've been champing for you to one day run this country, but maybe just running the city will be enough to be your legacy

event_label: Chatter That Matters podcast with Tony Chapman
source_quote: Had a powerful conversation with my friend Tony Chapman at @chatterthatmatters about the future of Toronto, including the dream of homeownership.

quote_text: The idea of homeownership is still a big part of the Canadian dream. And there's a lot of us out there swinging with both arms, who are not ready to give up on that.
speaker: Brad Bradford

quote_text: The way that Toronto was governed from a zoning and planning perspective for the past twenty years since amalgamation, that is not working anymore.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States bike infrastructure should be approached case-by-case, with community engagement and trust-building, not as a black-and-white issue.
source_quote: Smart and sensible bike infrastructure requires time and hard work to build trust... we need to plan carefully and engage with community on a case-by-case basis.

summary: States the Danforth bike lanes process involved community engagement while the Bloor West process did not.
source_quote: We put in the work on Danforth. That didn't happen on Bloor West.

summary: States residents' concerns on bike lanes should be listened to rather than ignored.
source_quote: We need to listen to residents - not ignore their concerns and gaslight them.

summary: States support for safe and sensible bike lanes built case-by-case, not a blanket position for or against.
source_quote: I don't think anyone on this call here this morning would say no bike lanes anywhere ever. It's about safe and sensible bike lanes.

summary: States the Bloor West bike lane process lacked the community engagement work that was done on Danforth.
source_quote: What's really unfortunate about Bloor West, is that work wasn't done. We doubled down on it in June when the mayor voted to continue it rather than the motion to remove it

summary: States progress in Toronto can only be made at the speed at which trust is built, and that trust has been undermined in Etobicoke.
source_quote: we can only make progress in the city of Toronto at the speed at which we can build trust. We have undermined people's trust, particularly out in Etobicoke

summary: Worked for a year and a half with business community, neighbourhoods, and residents associations before introducing Danforth bike lanes.
source_quote: I spent a year and a half working with the business community, working with the neighborhoods, working with residents associations before we introduce that.

summary: Introduced changes at a Danforth intersection including a dedicated right-hand turn lane.
source_quote: even recently making changes at one of the intersections where we introduced a dedicated right hand turn lane

summary: References a June vote where the mayor voted to continue Bloor West bike lanes rather than the motion to remove them.
source_quote: We doubled down on it in June when the mayor voted to continue it rather than the motion to remove it

quote_text: We can only make progress in the city of Toronto at the speed at which we can build trust.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States that condemnation alone is insufficient and calls for real action and leadership to address antisemitism in Toronto.
source_quote: Condemnation is needed, but not sufficient. We need real action and leadership to stamp out the awful Antisemitism that has taken root in Toronto.

summary: States the Vacant Home Tax program is fundamentally flawed because it requires homeowners to prove annually they live in their own homes.
source_quote: This program is fundamentally flawed. Placing the weight on homeowners to prove they live in their own homes each year is totally absurd.

summary: States over 160,000 residents were caught up in a system meant to target 8,000 units, indicating the system is broken.
source_quote: Last year, over 160,000 residents were caught up in a system meant to target just 8,000 units. This only proves one thing: the system is broken.

summary: States taxes make up 29% of the cost of a new home and opposes additional tax burdens on housing.
source_quote: Taxes already make up 29% of the cost of a new home. With historic property tax increases, a double-hit land transfer tax, and the cost of everything going up, the last thing folks want to worry about is another tax.

summary: States the Vacant Home Tax has not delivered the promised new homes coming onto the market.
source_quote: Because worst of all, it also isn't unlocking the new homes that were promised.

summary: Position that the Vacant Home Tax program should be cut unless the reverse-onus on homeowners is fixed.
source_quote: this program needs to be cut unless this reverse-onus on homeowners is fixed.

summary: States the program was sold to Torontonians on housing outcomes, not revenue, and housing outcomes have not materialized.
source_quote: this was sold to Torontonians on the premise that it was never about the revenue. It was about the housing outcome. We haven't seen the housing outcome.

summary: Calls for thoughtfulness in adding more taxes on housing in Toronto, described as the most expensive city in the country.
source_quote: we need to be very thoughtful when we are adding more taxes on housing units in the most expensive city in in the country.

summary: Called at City Council for an urgent halt to the Vacant Home Tax for 2025.
source_quote: Yesterday during Council, I called for an urgent halt to the Vacant Home Tax for 2025.

quote_text: We need to cut the hypocrisy, and focus on real policy outcomes - not just revenue generation.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States taxpayers deserve better services from the City.
source_quote: Taxpayers deserve better services from our City

pledge_text: Will keep fighting for improvements in public health and safety.
source_quote: I will keep fighting for improvements in public health and safety.

summary: Brought a motion to reinstate the 48-hour service standard for removing deceased animals; approved by Council.
source_quote: My motion to reinstate the 48-hour service standard for removing deceased animals was approved.

summary: States that without renegotiating the tripartite agreement, the future operations of the Billy Bishop airport are jeopardized because the main aircraft used (Dash 8 Q400) is no longer in production.
source_quote: the tripartite agreement specifies the type of aircraft that are allowed to be used at the airport and that the main commercial aircraft flown from the airport, the dash eight q 400 is literally no longer in production. And so if we cannot renegotiate the tripartite, you are effectively putting a nail in the coffin of the future operations of this airport.

summary: States that the Mayor's motions, which passed, are an attempt to avoid accountability and prevent further public consultation until 2027.
source_quote: The motions from the Mayor and her team - which passed today - are a clear attempt to avoid accountability and prevent any further public consultation from happening until 2027.

summary: States that Torontonians deserve honesty and transparency rather than vague statements and false promises.
source_quote: The people of Toronto deserve honesty and transparency, not false promises.

summary: Questioned the Mayor at council about her motion deleting the renegotiation of the tripartite airport agreement in 2025.
source_quote: Madam mayor, the original motion that was in front of us here today was to renegotiate the tripartite in 2025. Your motion that you just put in front of council deletes that.

quote_text: Vague statements and dodged questions won't keep our airport and economy thriving for the long term.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States Torontonians are paying more in taxes but getting less in services, and City Hall is not delivering value for money.
source_quote: Torontonians are paying more in taxes. They are getting less. We are promised improvements in services.

summary: States accountability questions should go to the city manager, head of parks, and Mayor Chow.
source_quote: these questions need to go right to the top of leadership at city hall. That is our city manager. That is the head of parks, and that is, of course, mayor Chao as well.

summary: States GPS data alone is insufficient; the work taxpayers pay for must actually be completed.
source_quote: GPS data is obviously not enough. When we're paying the salaries, when we're paying for those jobs, we need to make sure that the work is being completed.

summary: References Mayor Chow's tax increase, stating it was made with a promise of better services that is not being delivered.
source_quote: this comes on the back of Olivia Chao's record breaking tax increase that was made with the promise of seeing better services.

pledge_text: Pledges to fight for accountability and value for money at City Hall by pushing the bureaucracy and the mayor.
source_quote: my job in terms of ensuring that we have accountability at City Hall is pushing the bureaucracy, pushing the mayor, and making sure that we're achieving value for money for taxpayers.
specifics: Raising as a top topic of discussion at council this week.

pledge_text: Pledges to demand accountability and fight for quality city services for Torontonians.
source_quote: I'm here to demand accountability and fight for getting the quality services Torontonians deserve—no more excuses.

quote_text: We're paying more. We're getting less. City Hall has to do better.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States Toronto is falling short on basic services, citing overflowing waste bins and neglected facilities in parks.
source_quote: Right now, Toronto is falling short on delivering basic services. We see it with the overflowing waste bins and neglected facilities in our parks.

summary: States a recent Auditor General report shows systemic issues including crews clocking out early and parking in plazas instead of maintaining parks.
source_quote: a recent Auditor General report shows systemic issues. Crews clocking out early, and spending hours each day parked in plazas instead of maintaining parks.

summary: States Mayor Chow gave Torontonians a historically high tax increase this year and residents should expect better services.
source_quote: Mayor Chow gave Torontonians a historically high tax increase this year. People should expect better services - which means it's essential that our City officials prioritize effective performance and value-for-money.

summary: States the city must demand better performance and accountability from city officials.
source_quote: We must demand better performance and accountability. Residents - taxpayers - expect it.

summary: States there is a systematic issue at the City of Toronto in ensuring value for money.
source_quote: I think there is a systematic issue at the city of Toronto, making sure that we are getting value for money in some of these instances.

summary: States ongoing collective bargaining negotiations should include performance incentives and measurement against service standards, not only compensation.
source_quote: there are incentives for performance, that that is something that we're looking at very carefully. This can't just be a negotiation about how how much more money everybody's gonna get paid. We need to we need to measure this stuff against the results, the service standards that we wanna see in our parks, in our public facilities.

summary: Acknowledges many city staff work hard, while stating workers should show up and do the job they are paid for.
source_quote: there's a lot of really fantastic city staff out there. A lot of them work really hard, but these numbers are quite damning. And and, you know, at the end of the day, you gotta show up and do the job that you're being paid for.

quote_text: This can't just be a negotiation about how much more money everybody's gonna get paid. We need to measure this stuff against the results, the service standards that we wanna see in our parks, in our public facilities.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States Toronto's basic city services need a serious upgrade, citing 19 days of a decomposing raccoon awaiting pickup.
source_quote: 19 days of a decomposing raccoon (data from one resident's email) is a clear sign that our city's basic services need a serious upgrade.

summary: States Torontonians shouldn't have to watch dead animals decompose for weeks.
source_quote: Torontonians shouldn't be watching dead animals slowly decompose for weeks on end.

summary: Brought a motion at City Council calling to reinstate the 48-hour service standard for dead animal pickup.
source_quote: My motion at Council this week calls to reinstate the 48 service standard.

summary: Expresses solidarity with the Jewish community, remembering victims of October 7 and calling for the release of remaining hostages.
source_quote: We remember the 1200 victims. More than 200 innocents taken hostage. More than 100 still kept in captivity. In dark times, we find strength together. You are not alone.

source_quote: Yesterday, we stood as thousands strong at the @cijainfo and @UJAFederation Vigil to send a clear message.

source_quote: I started this solemn day by joining morning prayers at @chabadonbayview. Together, we remembered and prayed for the victims and survivors of the October 7 massacre.

summary: States that protests targeting neighborhoods and attacks on businesses and schools in Toronto are unacceptable.
source_quote: In Toronto, we've seen protests targeting neighborhoods and attacks on businesses and schools. This is unacceptable.

summary: States solidarity with the Jewish community on the anniversary of October 7 and condemns the rise in antisemitism.
source_quote: What followed in the days, weeks, and months since has been a disgusting wave of antisemitism that has swept across Canada, and it plays out on the streets in big cities like here in Toronto.

pledge_text: Pledges to continue fighting against antisemitism and to defend Canadian values of peace and tolerance.
source_quote: I will never give up the fight against Antisemitism, and in defence of our shared Canadian values of peace and tolerance.

pledge_text: Pledges to always stand in solidarity with the Jewish community in the collective fight against antisemitism.
source_quote: I will always be there to stand in solidarity in our collective fight against antisemitism.

quote_text: You are not forgotten, and you are not alone.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: Calls for the immediate release of hostages held by Hamas.
source_quote: we offered our prayers for those who are still being held hostage by the Hamas terrorists. We call for their immediate release.

topic_focus: Memorial for victims of the October 7th attacks

summary: States opposition to hate and antisemitism, expressing solidarity with victims of October 7th and calling for hostages' return.
source_quote: Together we stand against hate and antisemitism.

event_label: Interfaith coalition remembrance for October 7th victims and survivors
topic_focus: Remembrance of October 7th victims, solidarity against antisemitism, call for hostages to return
source_quote: an interfaith coalition of leaders came together to remember the victims and survivors of the October 7th massacres, to stand in solidarity, and to call for hostages to come home

summary: States commitment to standing with the Jewish community against antisemitism.
source_quote: As the fight against antisemitism continues, I'll always have your back.

pledge_text: Pledges ongoing support to Toronto's Jewish community in the fight against antisemitism.
source_quote: As the fight against antisemitism continues, I'll always have your back.

event_label: #BringThemHomeNow Rally
topic_focus: Solidarity with Jewish community and families of hostages; opposing antisemitism
source_quote: I was honoured to stand with Toronto's Jewish community, families of hostages, and allies today at the Bathurst and Sheppard #BringThemHomeNow Rally.

summary: States Mayor Chow should be transparent about 2025 property tax estimates that city staff have already produced.
source_quote: City staff have an estimate, but Mayor Chow isn't sharing it. After last year's historic 9.5% hike, taxpayers deserve transparency from City leaders.

summary: Characterizes the 2024 property tax increase as a record-breaking hike of nearly 10% during an affordability crisis.
source_quote: Amidst an affordability crisis here in Toronto, the mayor hit everyone with a record breaking tax increase, nearly 10%.

summary: States the mayor should be honest and transparent with Torontonians about the cost of living in the city.
source_quote: The mayor should be honest and transparent with Torontonians about how expensive it's gonna be to live in this city.

pledge_text: Will keep pushing for a more affordable Toronto.
source_quote: I will keep pushing until we have a more affordable Toronto.

pledge_text: Will participate in the city budget consultation process.
source_quote: If you want more accountability from your elected officials, please engage in the budget consultation process… That's where I'm gonna be.

source_quote: Thanks Teresa, Ramon, Phil, Onette and everyone involved for your efforts in building a more inclusive and prosperous economy.

source_quote: Yesterday I meet with the team behind @placatvtoronto's new project, Pathways to Prosperity. This program is helping newcomers in Canada develop skills and get jobs in construction, hospitality and more.

source_quote: On Sunday, we celebrated the opening of the new garden at St. Aidan's in the Beach.

summary: States that true reconciliation requires both truth and action.
source_quote: True reconciliation requires both truth and action.

summary: Attended the opening of the Spirit Garden at Nathan Phillips Square honouring survivors and victims of Ontario's 18 former residential schools, marking the City's response to TRC Call to Action #82.
source_quote: We came together this morning at Nathan Phillips Square to honour the survivors and victims of Ontario's 18 former residential schools with the opening of the Spirit Garden.

event_label: Opening of the Spirit Garden — National Day for Truth and Reconciliation
topic_focus: Truth and Reconciliation; honouring residential school survivors and victims
source_quote: We came together this morning at Nathan Phillips Square to honour the survivors and victims of Ontario's 18 former residential schools with the opening of the Spirit Garden.

summary: States there is a disconnect between Toronto's leadership and community, citing a Maru poll.
source_quote: Unfortunately, Toronto is facing such a disconnect between leadership and community.

summary: Criticizes spending $150M on a 2-km bike path while basic needs go unaddressed.
source_quote: people see a feel-good announcement about spending $150M on a 2-km bike path while more basic needs go unaddressed

summary: States the city needs leadership to rebuild confidence and public trust.
source_quote: We need leadership to rebuild confidence and public trust, and ensure Torontonians feel confident in building a life in this great city once again.

summary: States that ending exclusionary zoning and expanding multiplex housing options in Toronto sets a precedent for the province and country.
source_quote: We're now in a position where we have been able to eliminate exclusionary zoning and provide lots of new types of housing which will build going forward in the neighbourhood. So this is precedent setting here in Toronto. It's precedent setting in the province and across the country.

summary: Supports the Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods multiplex policy and frames it as building a more inclusive and affordable Toronto.
source_quote: Together, we're building a more inclusive and affordable Toronto for all.

summary: Recognized City Planning's Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods Multiplex team at committee for winning the OPPI 2024 Vision Award of Merit.
source_quote: I just wanted to be here in committee today and thank everyone for their hard work and leadership.

summary: States the Vacant Home Tax places the burden on 800,000 Toronto households to prove they live in their homes, treating homeowners as 'guilty until proven innocent'.
source_quote: The Mayor and staff still haven't addressed the fundamental issue of the Vacant Home Tax, which places the burden on 800,000 households in Toronto to prove they live in their homes. This approach deems every homeowner guilty until proven innocent, and keeps the reverse-onus on them.

summary: States the Mayor should prioritize supply-side housing solutions and reduce red tape rather than increasing taxes.
source_quote: The Mayor should prioritize supply-side solutions, reducing red tape and easing the burden on homeowners, rather than increasing taxes and complicating the process.

summary: Calls for axing the Vacant Home Tax until its fundamental flaw is fixed.
source_quote: Until this fundamental flaw is fixed, we should Axe the Tax.

summary: States that increasing taxes and fees has been the default setting of the current mayoral administration.
source_quote: here we are another year later, which seems the deep be the default setting of this administration to increase taxes, to increase fees

quote_text: Until this fundamental flaw is fixed, we should Axe the Tax.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States congestion and traffic is the top issue he hears about, and it is City Hall's responsibility to fix, not the province's.
source_quote: Congestion and traffic is the number one issue I hear about - and it's up to City Hall to fix it, not the province.

summary: States the Mayor and Council need to listen to Torontonians about how they get around the city, including on construction management and bike lane placement.
source_quote: the Mayor and Council need to actually listen to the people of Toronto about how they get around the city. This goes for how to manage construction projects, and also for where bike lanes make sense and where they don't.

summary: States bike lanes should not be everywhere; placement decisions should be made with common sense and input from communities and small businesses.
source_quote: We just don't have the leadership on that file to listen to communities, listen to small business, and have a better understanding where we're gonna build the bike lanes. They can't be everywhere. Where are we gonna build them? Where do they make sense?

summary: States the province does not need to make decisions about specific Toronto bike lanes (e.g., Bloor West, the Kingsway); the City has the tools to decide.
source_quote: Need the the province to tell me that we shouldn't have a bike lane on Bloor West or we shouldn't have a bike lane on the Kingsway. I mean, that is common sense. We don't need the province to fix that for us. We need to have common sense of leadership at city hall. We have all the tools available to us here in this building to make those types of decisions.

quote_text: Leadership starts with listening and with some common sense.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States Toronto needs significantly more purpose-built rental housing as the city grows.
source_quote: As Toronto grows, we need a lot more purpose-built rental.

summary: States City Hall needs to speed up approvals and ensure project economics work so new housing can proceed.
source_quote: That means making sure City Hall is speeding up approvals and doing our part to make sure the numbers work for new projects to go ahead.

pledge_text: Continue working to get shovels in the ground for new housing in the years ahead.

source_quote: We need to keep getting shovels in the ground to ensure we have the homes we need in the years ahead.

summary: Supports creating a Congestion Relief Commissioner / 'Traffic Tsar' / office of congestion management to coordinate construction projects across Toronto.
source_quote: For more than a year, I've been calling for a Congestion Relief Commissioner to coordinate and prioritize all the different construction projects across Toronto.

summary: States the city needs better front-end management of construction projects rather than band-aid solutions after the fact.
source_quote: we need someone to do a much better job on the front end of managing these projects, rather than offering band-aid solutions after the fact.

summary: States that without change, Toronto's traffic management will remain a cycle of 'hurry up and wait.'
source_quote: Until this changes, Toronto's traffic management strategy will be a constant cycle of hurry up and wait.

summary: Authored an op-ed in the Toronto Star on tackling Toronto's congestion crisis.
source_quote: Read my latest op-ed for the @thetorontostar on how we can tackle the city's congestion crisis head on.

summary: States that trust and community collaboration can successfully advance supportive housing projects and help tackle the housing crisis.
source_quote: This project is proof that trust and collaboration can make a real difference in our community and successfully contribute to tackling the housing crisis.

summary: States that more needs to be done on housing affordability beyond the Cedarvale project.
source_quote: Although Cedarvale is a success we should all be proud of, more needs to be done.

pledge_text: Will continue to fight for housing affordability until every Torontonian has a place to call home.
source_quote: I will continue to fight for housing affordability until every Torontonian has a place to call home.

summary: Supported and championed the Cedarvale supportive housing project, engaging community amid opposition; project now houses 59 people.
source_quote: In 2021, I faced significant opposition to building the Cedarvale supportive housing project in our community... Today, 59 people have a home at Cedarvale, and I’m proud to say we have zero complaints from neighbours.

summary: States that Legions have a mission to protect and share the stories of veterans.
source_quote: Our Legions are not only places to gather - they have a mission to protect and share the stories of our veterans.

event_label: Legion Week and Battle of Britain anniversary at Branch 11
location: Royal Canadian Legion Branch 11, East York
source_quote: Honoured to have joined Branch 11 for a meaningful start to Legion Week and the Battle of Britain anniversary.

summary: States Toronto congestion has worsened and it is harder to get around by car, transit, or bike.
source_quote: Torontonians know congestion has never been worse. It's never been harder to get around this city, whether you're driving, taking transit, or riding a bike.

summary: Argues Mayor Chow has reversed positions on Gardiner reconstruction, Spadina streetcar track work, and DVP off-ramp work in the past three months.
source_quote: In just the last three months, Mayor Chow has had to flip-flop on her approach to: ❌ Gardiner reconstruction ❌ Spadina streetcar track work ❌ DVP Off-ramp work

summary: States better construction coordination needs to begin at the top of city government and be done right the first time.
source_quote: We need to get serious. Better coordination needs to begin at the top, and get it right the first time.

summary: States the Mayor's congestion announcement relied on cherry-picked statistics that do not reflect underlying traffic problems.
source_quote: a few cherry-picked statistics don't mean the underlying traffic issues have actually been solved

summary: States dedicated bus lanes on Spadina will improve bus travel time but not travel time for other road users on Spadina.
source_quote: While adding dedicated bus lanes on Spadina Avenue is going to improve travel time for those folks that are on the bus. It's not gonna improve travel time for everybody else using Spadina Avenue.

summary: States moving people and goods and keeping citizens safe are core competencies of local government that have declined over the past year.
source_quote: Making sure that people can get around this city is table stakes for local government. This is the basic core competency of the job... both of those things have taken a real dive, over the past year

pledge_text: Will continue fighting for common-sense solutions to reduce commute times for Torontonians.
source_quote: I will continue to fight for common-sense solutions to get Torontonians home faster at the end of their day.

pledge_text: Will keep fighting for better construction coordination and prioritizing moving people in the city.
specifics: Better coordination of construction projects; prioritization of moving people
source_quote: I'm gonna keep fighting for better coordination and the prioritization of moving people here in this city so you could get back to work and back to your family at the end of the day faster.

quote_text: Making sure that people can get around this city is table stakes for local government. This is the basic core competency of the job.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States the City's handling of construction projects is poorly managed and needs to be addressed.

summary: States minimizing traffic impacts of construction must be a top priority for the City and Mayor.
source_quote: Minimizing the traffic impacts of necessary construction projects needs to be the first priority for the City and the Mayor - not an afterthought.

summary: States the Mayor has had to change plans on the Gardiner, Spadina, and DVP off-ramp in the last three months.
source_quote: In just the last three months, the Mayor has had to scramble to change the plan on the Gardiner, Spadina, and now the DVP off-ramp.

summary: States projects should not tie up every available parallel route, and better planning is needed.

summary: States traffic coordination must be a priority in all major construction projects.

summary: States the Mayor should be calling in bureaucrats and not signing off on haphazard construction approaches.

summary: References pushing the Mayor for months to get the Gardiner construction to 24/7 operations.

summary: States the City failed to anticipate the traffic impact of the DVP lane closure.

summary: States current city hall administration does not prioritize moving goods and people or recognize quality-of-life impacts of traffic.

summary: Supports doing construction but with better staging and coordination to reduce traffic impact.

summary: Calls for leadership that prioritizes congestion and building planning so Torontonians can get home faster.
source_quote: We need leadership that prioritizes this so that Torontonians can get home to their families faster.

quote_text: Torontonians are suffering for it. And I think they're getting frustrated, and they're kinda sick and tired of it. We have to do a better job.

summary: Held community conversation on proposed modular supportive housing development at Trenton and Cedarvale; collecting feedback via online survey and CLC.
source_quote: Tough, but necessary, conversation last night on the proposed modular supportive housing development at Trenton and Cedarvale... We're working closely with the community to address concerns on safety, parking, and how we can best support our new neighbours.

summary: States that agencies across Toronto, including Metrolinx, take a reactive approach to communities, and that engaging local experts is critical to doing work right the first time.
source_quote: The reactive approach to Small's Creek from Metrolinx is emblematic of the approach that agencies across Toronto take with communities. Engaging and working with the community, the local experts, is critical to ensuring that the work is done right the first time.

summary: Supports preservation of the Small's Creek ravine and views the Metrolinx working group and 2000-tree planting as a positive step.
source_quote: Metrolinx will be setting up a #SmallsCreek working group with local stakeholders and planting 2000 trees in our community... this is a big step in the right direction.

summary: Advocacy on Small's Creek resulted in Metrolinx agreeing to set up a working group with local stakeholders and plant 2000 trees in the community.
source_quote: Metrolinx will be setting up a #SmallsCreek working group with local stakeholders and planting 2000 trees in our community.

summary: States that permanent, supportive housing is a critical, long-term solution for homelessness.
source_quote: Building people up and providing permanent, supportive housing is a critical, long-term solution for homelessness.

summary: Supports the proposed supportive, modular housing development on Trenton and engaging the community on it.
source_quote: Out on Trenton this morning talking to neighbours about the proposed supportive, modular housing development.

summary: Canvassed neighbours on Trenton about the proposed supportive modular housing development, distributing information and inviting them to a community meeting.
source_quote: Out on Trenton this morning talking to neighbours about the proposed supportive, modular housing development. Listening to concerns from the community, dropping off more information about the project, and inviting them to our meeting on Monday, March 8th, at 7pm.

event_label: Community canvass on Trenton re: proposed supportive modular housing
source_quote: Out on Trenton this morning talking to neighbours about the proposed supportive, modular housing development.

event_label: Community meeting on supportive modular housing project
location: Virtual / register at link in bio
source_quote: inviting them to our meeting on Monday, March 8th, at 7pm

quote_text: Building people up and providing permanent, supportive housing is a critical, long-term solution for homelessness.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States the engagement process for the Trenton and Cedarvale modular housing site has not been up to standard.
source_quote: I've heard from many of you that the engagement process for this site hasn't been up to standard. I agree.

summary: States notices didn't go out early enough and signs should have been posted on site; the City is playing catch up.
source_quote: Notices didn't go out early enough and signs should have gone up on site. Unfortunately, the City's playing catch up while community concern and misinformation spreads.

summary: Supports building supportive housing rather than shelters, with supports in place to ensure success.
source_quote: We need to stop building shelters, and start building housing - and we need to make sure we have the supports in place to ensure they are successful.

summary: States there is a housing crisis with people living in encampments and dying on the streets, and the accelerated process reflects that urgency.
source_quote: We have a housing crisis, people living in encampments, and folks dying on our streets... The speed of the process is intended to reflect the urgency of the crisis.

summary: Opposes stigmatization of vulnerable residents and also opposes dismissing community concerns.
source_quote: I will not tolerate stigmatization of our most vulnerable residents and I will also not tolerate dismissing the concerns that real people in our communities have.

pledge_text: Will hold an urgent community meeting on March 8 to address concerns about the Trenton and Cedarvale site, in addition to the March 17 consultation meeting.
specifics: Urgent meeting March 8, 2021; consultation meeting March 17, 2021; registration at tiny.cc/Trenton
source_quote: I've requested an urgent meeting to address the community's concerns on Monday March 8th. This is in addition to the consultation meeting planned for MArch 17th.

summary: Brought a motion at Planning and Housing Committee ensuring public consultations occur before any final decision on zoning changes for the Trenton and Cedarvale modular housing site.
source_quote: My motion at committee today was adopted unanimously and ensures that public consultations take place before any final decision gets made on zoning changes.

quote_text: We need to stop building shelters, and start building housing - and we need to make sure we have the supports in place to ensure they are successful.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States there is a critical need to provide housing for the most vulnerable, alongside a need for appropriate community engagement on supportive housing proposals.
source_quote: While we can all agree on the critical need to provide housing for our most vulnerable, there is also a need for appropriate community engagement.

summary: States community engagement on the Trenton and Cedarvale proposal should focus on the 'how' — including parking around a community hub and safety for those involved.
source_quote: The engagement ahead of us has to focus on the "how". Addressing parking around a community hub and how we're going to be keeping everyone involved safe are critical aspects of the "how" conversation.

summary: States the community's voice as local experts is essential to getting the supportive housing process right.
source_quote: the community's voice as the local experts is essential to ensure that we get it right.

summary: Convening a community meeting on March 8 regarding the proposed supportive housing development at Trenton and Cedarvale, with staff available to answer questions.
source_quote: Join me on Monday, March 8th, for a community meeting on the proposal. We'll also have staff on the line to answer questions and address concerns.

event_label: Community meeting on proposed supportive housing at Trenton and Cedarvale
location: Trenton and Cedarvale, Beaches—East York (virtual meeting)
topic_focus: Supportive housing proposal and community engagement
source_quote: Join me on Monday, March 8th, for a community meeting on the proposal. We'll also have staff on the line to answer questions and address concerns.

quote_text: We're here because we're taking poverty seriously, and we're serious about helping the members of this community that need it.
speaker: Brad Bradford

event_label: #CrushCOVID: Ride for Mind discussion (virtual event)
source_quote: Coming up on Monday night at 7pm! Join us for a discussion on the growing mental health impacts of the pandemic and how supporting the #CrushCOVID: Ride for Mind will make a tangible difference in our community.

summary: States CafeTO provides support for small businesses and a safe way for communities to enjoy summer.
source_quote: Bringing it back to give communities a safe way to enjoy their summer and provide some extra support for our mom-and-pops during these tough times.

summary: Announces that registration for the CafeTO program is open.
source_quote: Registration for the #CafeTO program is now open!

summary: States that rising insurance premiums, denied coverage, and claim hurdles are adding to the COVID burden on small businesses.
source_quote: Massive increases in insurance premiums, coverage being denied & hurdles to making claims are adding to the #COVID burden on our small businesses.

summary: States that the Province can take action on insurance rules affecting small businesses.
source_quote: @fordnationdougford and the Province can take action.

summary: Joined with the Toronto Association of Business Improvement Areas to request changes to provincial insurance rules to support local business.
source_quote: With the Toronto Association of Business Improvement Areas, I'm asking for changes to insurance rules to support local business.

summary: Supports new modular supportive housing project in Beaches-East York and Willowdale.
source_quote: Today I joined Mayor @johntory and my fellow elected officials for an important and positive announcement welcoming vital new supportive housing opportunities in Beaches-East York & Willowdale.

summary: States there is an urgent need for housing requiring quick action.
source_quote: Moving quickly to address the urgent need for housing.

summary: Joined Mayor John Tory and other elected officials to announce ~64 modular supportive housing units proposed for parking lot at Trenton Ave and Cedarvale Ave, targeted for occupancy by end of 2021.
source_quote: Currently, an estimated 64 modular supportive housing units would be built on the parking lot at Trenton Avenue and Cedarvale Avenue, with the goal of having them ready for occupancy by the end of 2021.

event_label: Modular supportive housing announcement with Mayor John Tory
source_quote: Today I joined Mayor @johntory and my fellow elected officials for an important and positive announcement welcoming vital new supportive housing opportunities in Beaches-East York & Willowdale.

event_label: Virtual community meeting on laneway improvements around Main Street TTC Station
source_quote: Coming up Wednesday evening! From 6-8pm, join me and the @lanewayproject to discuss some upcoming improvements being made to laneways around the Main Street #TTC Station.

summary: States that advancing Toronto's skateboarding strategy is necessary to make healthy outdoor activities more accessible.
source_quote: Moving forward on Toronto's skateboarding strategy is a necessary step to make healthy outdoor activities more accessible.

summary: States that developing new skateparks and maintaining existing ones are critical to encouraging healthy lifestyles.
source_quote: Advancing the development of new skateparks and maintaining our current ones are critical pieces of continuing that important work and incentivizing healthy lifestyles.

summary: Observes that the pandemic has highlighted the importance of safe ways to get active outdoors.
source_quote: The pandemic has highlighted the importance of providing these safe ways to #GetActive and we can do more to encourage this.

summary: States that Toronto's music industry needs help to recover from the pandemic if the city wants to continue calling itself a music city.
source_quote: Toronto was a music city before the pandemic and if we want to continue calling ourselves that, we need to help the industry recover.

summary: Supports creation of a new property tax subclass for live music venues that would reduce property taxes for eligible locations by up to 50%.
source_quote: In Toronto we're moving forward on the creation of a new property tax subclass for live music venues, reducing property taxes for eligible locations by up to 50%.

summary: States that recovery of Toronto's music industry will require support from all levels of government.
source_quote: there is so much potential to make a comeback, but we need the support of all levels of government to make this happen.

summary: Voted in 2019 to Strengthen Toronto's Night Economy, addressing zoning, identifying new venue locations, and supporting patrons with public restrooms and accessible transit.
source_quote: In 2019, we voted to Strengthen Toronto's Night Economy by addressing zoning issues, identifying new locations for venues, and looking for opportunities to better support patrons with public restrooms and more accessible transit.

summary: Moving forward on creating a new property tax subclass for live music venues to reduce property taxes by up to 50% for eligible locations.
source_quote: In Toronto we're moving forward on the creation of a new property tax subclass for live music venues, reducing property taxes for eligible locations by up to 50%.

quote_text: I want to see the Toronto music industry come out stronger than before.
speaker: Brad Bradford

summary: States the 2021 Toronto budget focused on responding to pandemic challenges and finding efficiencies without affecting services.
source_quote: We dove into the balance sheets to find some $573 million in savings and offsets to do our work more efficiently without affecting services, and stay focused on using every available dollar to help with recovery and support.

summary: States the budget makes investments in equity across three areas: community safety, financial supports, and public transit.
source_quote: We're making critical investment in equity in three key areas: community safety, financial supports, and public transit.

summary: States the pandemic exposed long-standing inequality and the budget invests in programs to support recovery and a more equitable Toronto.
source_quote: 2020 forced us to face the long-standing inequality epidemic in light of the public health pandemic. Through the budget the City's investing in the programs and supports to empower our recovery and build back a more sustainable and equitable Toronto.

summary: Council adopted the 2021 Toronto Budget; Bradford served as Vice-Chair of the Budget Committee for a third year.
source_quote: Council met today to adopt the 2021 Toronto Budget. This was my third year as Vice-Chair of the City's Budget Committee

summary: States that as vaccine supplies increase, doses need to be distributed quickly and efficiently to Canadians to support recovery.
source_quote: As supplies increase, we need to quickly and efficiently get shots out of freezers and into the arms of Canadians to begin our recovery in earnest.

summary: Met with East End healthcare providers to discuss preparations for a mass vaccine rollout.
source_quote: Met with the incredible team of #EastEnd healthcare providers yesterday to discuss the preparations for a mass vaccine rollout.

event_label: Meeting with East End healthcare providers on vaccine rollout preparations
source_quote: Met with the incredible team of #EastEnd healthcare providers yesterday to discuss the preparations for a mass vaccine rollout.

summary: Supports extending Toronto's lockdown by two weeks to protect vulnerable residents while awaiting broader vaccine rollout.
source_quote: A tough decision, but the one we need to make. We have to do everything we can to protect our vulnerable while we wait for a broad vaccine rollout.

summary: States the lockdown extension will be hard on small businesses and mental health, but reopening too quickly could lead back into another lockdown.
source_quote: Continuing with another 2 week lockdown will be incredibly hard. The impacts on our small business community and the mental health of Torontonians cannot be understated. However, opening too quickly could have equally devastating effects and lead us right back into another lockdown.

summary: Supports continuing and strengthening supports for local businesses and communities during the extended lockdown.
source_quote: These few extra weeks will save lives, but we need to continue and strengthen our supports for local businesses and communities.

summary: States that lockdowns and extended isolation have had devastating impacts on mental health.
source_quote: Over the last year, we've seen firsthand the devestating impacts that lockdowns and extended isolation have had on mental health.

pledge_text: Will cycle 24 straight hours to raise funds for Michael Garron Hospital's mental health programs in CrushCOVID: Ride for Mind.
specifics: 24 hours of cycling; supports Transitional Youth Program and new mental health facilities at Michael Garron Hospital; livestream March 12th
source_quote: I'm getting back in the saddle for another 24 straight hours of cycling in support of @michaelgarronhospital's fight for mental health in #CrushCOVID: Ride for Mind.

summary: Participated in 24-hour cycling fundraiser for Michael Garron Hospital during the first months of the pandemic.
source_quote: It was incredible last year to be joined by folks from all across the world, as our global community came together to support those who needed it during the first few months of the pandemic.

event_label: CrushCOVID: Ride for Mind
topic_focus: Mental health fundraising for Michael Garron Hospital
source_quote: I'm getting back in the saddle for another 24 straight hours of cycling in support of @michaelgarronhospital's fight for mental health in #CrushCOVID: Ride for Mind.

summary: States the decision to close the SRT in 2023, seven years before the Scarborough Subway is expected to be complete, is tough and stems from decades of delays and politicization of transit.
source_quote: The decision to close down the SRT in 2023, 7 years before the expected completion of the Scarborough Subway, is tough. It's the result of decades of delays and the politicization of transit.

summary: States the City and transit riders shouldn't carry the cost of transit politics; Province should help fund additional buses required by the SRT closure.
source_quote: We need help from the Province to fund the additional buses required from this decision - the City and transit riders shouldn't carry the cost of transit politics.

summary: Supports adding more bus priority lanes, signal priority, and new routes to keep buses moving and respect transit riders' time during the SRT replacement.
source_quote: To respect transit riders' time we need to look at adding more bus priority lanes, signal priority and new routes and keep buses moving.

summary: States the Fair Pass program makes the TTC more equitable and accessible.
source_quote: The Fair Pass program makes the TTC more equitable and accessible.

summary: Characterizes a federal announcement as a step in the right direction and expresses hope the Province will follow.
source_quote: Federal announcement today is a big step in the right direction and I hope we can count on the Province to do the same.

pledge_text: Begin work now on bus priority lanes, signal priority, and new routes to replace SRT service efficiently.
specifics: One bus every minute at peak times to replace the SRT; work needs to start now ahead of SRT closure.
source_quote: We'll need to run one bus every minute to replace the SRT at peak times... With the SRT slated to close in 2021, this work needs to start now.

pledge_text: Integrate the Fair Pass program with PRESTO to make sign-up easier, and work with intergovernmental partners to improve access.
specifics: PRESTO integration; intergovernmental coordination on access.
source_quote: We're integrating the program with PRESTO to make it easier to sign up and working with intergovernmental partners to improve access for those who need it most.

summary: States that Toronto's main streets need to survive the next few months until vaccines are more broadly available and the city can fully reopen.
source_quote: Need to ensure that our main streets survive these critical next few months until vaccines can be more broadly and we can fully reopen.

summary: Describes the partial reopening of non-essential businesses at 25% capacity in lockdown regions as a breath of fresh air for struggling small businesses.
source_quote: A breath of fresh air for the small businesses that have been struggling through this lockdown.

summary: States CafeTO was a lifeline for small businesses, citing nearly 70% saying they wouldn't have survived without it.
source_quote: Not only was it a lifeline for small businesses - nearly 70% say they wouldn't have survived without it - it brought some normalcy back for residents

pledge_text: Bring back the CafeTO program for 2021 with improvements based on business and BIA feedback.
specifics: CafeTO 2.0 for 2021 with program improvements
source_quote: After an incredibly successful run in 2020, we're bringing back the #CafeTO program for 2021!

pledge_text: Allow patios to open earlier, on the Victoria Day Long Weekend if public health allows.
specifics: Victoria Day Long Weekend opening, contingent on public health
source_quote: We're allowing patios to open earlier, on the Victoria Day Long Weekend if public health allows.

pledge_text: Make applications easier for businesses and install patios quicker after approvals.
source_quote: We're also making applications easier for businesses and working to get patios installed quicker after approvals.

pledge_text: Explore opportunities for retail stores to set up in curb areas when patios aren't open during the day.
specifics: Daytime curb-area use by retail when patios closed
source_quote: I've also asked staff to look at opportunities for retail stores to set-up in curb areas when patios aren't open during the day.

pledge_text: TTC will resolve conflicts with night bus service along the Danforth and other areas.
specifics: Night bus service along Danforth and other areas
source_quote: The TTC will also be resolving some conflicts with night bus service along the Danforth and some other areas
